title: Clinical Screening for Undernutrition in the Elderly Person With Loss of Autonomy : a Feasibility and Acceptability Syudy
official: Clinical Screening for Undernutrition in the Elderly Person With Loss of Autonomy : a Feasibility and Acceptability Syudy
summary: Pilot feasibility and acceptability study, using a prospective, descriptive, mixed-methods, multicentre design, conducted in four Home Care Services in the region. Five social and healthcare support workers will be recruited at each centre to visit older adults in their homes, measure their weight, assess their food intake and implement the malnutrition screening protocol.
conditions: Education on Feeding and Health Status
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Person aged 70 or over,
* Elderly person living at home,
* Elderly person followed by a home autonomy service (SAD)
* Elderly person followed at home by an Educational and Social Companion (AES) with or without meal delivery
* Elderly person receiving the APA (Personalized Autonomy Allowance),
* Elderly people with a loss of autonomy, with a GIR score between 3 and 4 (GIR 3: the elderly person needs help on a daily basis and several times a day for their bodily autonomy; GIR 4: the elderly person must be helped with washing and dressing),
* Elderly person able to read and write in French
* Elderly person who has received information about the protocol and has expressed non-opposition

Exclusion Criteria:

* Older adults with a diagnosis of cognitive impairment or dementia
* Elderly people who cannot be weighed (obesity, mobility problems, etc.),
* Pre-inclusion undernourished older adults
* Elderly person refusing to transmit information in the event of malnutrition to the attending physician
* Elderly person under curatorship, guardianship or safeguard of justice
